title: strided-alltoall-handoff-and-persistent-collective-scheduler
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads suffer intermittent stalls when small, frequent sharded exchanges (AllToAll/Reduce) contend on NCCL progress and stream ownership. Prior fixes focused on batching or changing communicator scopes but did not address steady-state micro-stalls caused by repeated collective handoffs and kernel preemption. This PR implements a strided alltoall handoff primitive alongside a persistent-collective scheduler that pins short collective phases to dedicated CUDA streams and staggers their invocation windows to reduce NCCL reinitialization and cross-stream synchronization hotspots.

Design summary: - Introduced 'StridedAllToAll' which aggregates many small tensor slices into stride-aware segments before submitting a single NCCL alltoall operation when contiguous GPU peer layout allows it. This reduces NCCL invocation count while preserving latency for large slices. - Added a PersistentCollectiveScheduler that keeps a pool of long-lived CUDA streams and NCCL communicators per tensor-parallel group. Scheduler uses a lightweight token-based handoff to queue collective windows and enforces non-overlapping kickoffs for groups that previously collided. - KV cache integration: when serving with KV sharding, the scheduler coalesces KV fetches into the same strided segments when access locality is detected, enabling combined comm+KV windows. A small heuristics engine decides when to fall back to the prior path to avoid increased latency for skewed access patterns. - Backward compatible: default is opt-in via runtime config flags (runtime.experimental.strided_alltoall and runtime.scheduler.persistent_collectives). We keep previous scheduler as a fallback.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced in PR body - [x] Unit tests for scheduler queueing and token handoff - [x] Microbenchmarks across 4xA100 and 8xA100 clusters - [x] KV cache interplay tests with synthetic access skew - [x] CI green and stress-run locally

Commits (high-level): - a1c9b6f Add StridedAllToAll primitive and unit tests - 7b4f2d3 PersistentCollectiveScheduler implementation and stream pool - e95d2b1 KV coalescing hooks and heuristics engine - 3f2b8a0 Integrate flags and runtime config parsing - 5c1d0ff Docs and quickstart for toggling during rollout

Files changed (high level): - rts/collectives/strided_alltoall.cpp/h - rts/scheduler/persistent_collective_scheduler.cpp/h - rts/kv/kv_coalesce.h - rts/config/runtime_flags.cpp - tests/collectives/strided_alltoall_test.cc - tests/scheduler/persistent_scheduler_smoke.cc - docs/rts/collectives.md - examples/bench/strided_alltoall_bench.py

Benchmark summary: - Baseline: 8xA100 TP=32, steady-state throughput 1200 tokens/s, 99th percentile token latency 58ms (small slice workload). - With StridedAllToAll + Persistent Scheduler: throughput increased to 1450 tokens/s (+20.8%), 99th percentile latency improved to 42ms (-27.6%), observed NCCL launch count reduced ~58% for the sampled timeframe. - KV-coalesced serving traces showed up to 18% additional reduction in p99 for mixed locality prompts. - Microbench stress tests (24-hour soak) show <0.1% increase in rare ordering regressions that are mitigated by a subsequent fallback path (enabled automatically under detected stalling).

Testing and CI: - CI: linux-build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-gpu (flaky -> rerun -> pass), lint (pass). - Added GPU-integration gating: a new job 'gpu-persistent-collectives' runs benchmarks on our perf-lab A100 pool during PR gating (was green).

Review thread (summary): - Michael Chen (reviewer): flagged potential deadlock if a scheduler token is lost during preemption; requested TTL and watchdog for tokens. - Author (Aisha): added a watchdog and re-queue path; added unit test to simulate scheduler preemption. - Sofia Martinez (reviewer): requested clearer metrics emitted for NCCL invocation rate; added telemetry counters (ncc_invoke_count, strided_merge_ops, scheduler_queue_depth). - Daniel Park (reviewer): suggested lowering default opt-in risk by shipping feature flags; PR implements flags and docs. - Security review (Ravi Patel): no new surface area; KV coalescing respects tenant boundaries and does not change key access privileges.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: New scheduler may hide regressions that only appear under >32k token workloads. Mitigation: feature rolled out using canary gate in Redwood Console, with automatic rollback if token latency increases >10% across canary. - Risk: Interaction with third-party NCCL wrappers. Mitigation: compatibility pings and fallbacks to legacy communicator mode if handshake fails.

Release notes: - Add opt-in strided all-to-all aggregation and persistent collective scheduler to reduce NCCL invocation count and p99 latency for multi-GPU tensor-parallel serving. Configuration flags and runtime telemetry added.

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main after final CI gate and bench verification.
